clue.text: Health ought not to be taken wholly for granted

indicators.note: only part of the words Health ought is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A warning not to assume you will always be in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for granted' reads as one phrase, but only 'granted' is the definition; 'for' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Granted, used as a conjunction, concedes a point just as the answer does: 'granted it rained, we still went'.

clue.text: Every American satellite passing over Pole, it's implied

parts.note: every means all
Io is a moon of Jupiter
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Every US satellite flying over the Pole carries some hidden suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing over' only describes the order of pieces in this down clue: IO comes above N.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference, something suggested rather than stated outright.

clue.text: Old player that you'd not want in your side finally vetoed by president

parts.words: that you'd not want in your side
parts.note: the idiom 'a thorn in your side' is a persistent annoyance

indicators.note: only the closing letter of vetoed is wanted

parts.note: last letter D
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A disruptive team member is eventually blocked by the club president.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Sybil Thorndike was a celebrated English stage actress of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Player is an old word for an actor, and Thorndike was a famous actress of the past.

clue.text: East Ender perhaps who aspires to appear on a musical show

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: one who hopes is a hoper

explanation.surface: A Cockney with dreams of performing in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to Cockneys, whose accent drops initial H, so 'hoper' is said 'oper'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music throughout, so it is a show built on music.

clue.text: Asian state prison turning over an informer

indicators.note: the word for prison is flipped end to end in this down answer

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
an is the indefinite article, A
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A state prison is overturned by a grass in an Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarat is a state on the western coast of India.

clue.text: Exercise in order to be cheerful?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pull-up raising the chin over a bar
second meaning: '...!' is the order you give someone to cheer up

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is an imperative: 'Chin up!' is what you say to tell someone to stay cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: The gym pull-up and the encouraging command 'keep your head high' share the same hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Sign of life in bather swimming before lunch?

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of bather moving about in the water

parts.note: taken as written
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: Checking a swimmer's pulse before a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges BATHER into HEARTB; 'before' puts it ahead of EAT, from lunch as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A detectable pulse shows a person is alive, so it is a vital sign.

clue.text: Outlet for soldier's natural aggression, as fighting is, primarily

indicators.note: the leading letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Fighting is a natural way for soldiers to release aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI runs shops and canteens for British service personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes is the British forces' retail and canteen organisation, a shop for troops.

clue.text: Irrational: a very loud English Trot going nowhere!

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An exasperated comment on a noisy English horse jogging on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A piaffe is a dressage movement in which the horse trots in place.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressage this movement is a trotting step performed without moving forward.

clue.text: Long-distance runner to stagger after cutting leg

indicators.note: the word for stagger has its tail cut off

parts.note: to stagger someone is to amaze them
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A marathon runner starts to totter after injuring a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a river here. In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is one of the world's longest rivers, and a river runs.

clue.text: Going places, free at last?

parts.note: loos are places where you go to the toilet

indicators.note: only the closing letter of free is used

parts.note: last letter E

explanation.surface: Someone finally released and able to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: being free at last means being at large.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means set free, unconfined, as an escaped animal is on the loose.

clue.text: Post articles, including place for Creole dish

parts.note: a jamb is an upright post of a door or window frame

indicators.note: the two articles hold the word for place between them

parts.note: A and A, two indefinite articles
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: Sending some writing that features a place to eat Creole food.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Louisiana rice dish with meat and seafood, a staple of Creole cooking.

clue.text: Old naval commander's spoken of Christmas holiday at sea?

indicators.note: the name is heard as a phrase said out loud

parts.note: a Santa cruise would be a festive voyage

explanation.surface: A former admiral is mentioned in connection with a festive cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: Álvaro de Bazán, Marquis of Santa Cruz, was a sixteenth-century Spanish admiral who planned the Armada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis of Santa Cruz commanded Spanish fleets, so he was a naval leader of long ago.

clue.text: Raffles maybe run once in newspaper, going back

indicators.note: the archaic word for run goes inside the reversed initials of the newspaper
the newspaper's initials are read from right to left

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times
hie is an old word for hurry

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a runner coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: FT turned round by 'going back' gives TF, and HIE goes inside it. A J Raffles is E W Hornung's gentleman burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles is a fictional cracksman, an example of someone who steals.

clue.text: Passage ancient poet largely avoided in recitation

indicators.note: most of the poet's name, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet

indicators.note: the word for avoided is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: ducked means dodged

explanation.surface: A poet's work mostly skipped when reading aloud in class.
explanation.definitionFit: An oviduct is the tube through which eggs pass from the ovary, a bodily channel.

clue.text: Evidently give not enough away, being so secretive?

parts.note: under means too little, as in underpaid
to hand is to give

explanation.surface: Holding something back makes someone seem furtive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evidently' warns of a cryptic reading: to under-hand would be to hand over too little.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are sly and done in secret, so the word means covert.

clue.text: A necessity to be originally called a dame

parts.note: née means born with the name, used for a maiden name
a DBE is a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A woman's maiden name is needed before she becomes a dame.
explanation.walkthrough: DBE is the British honour that makes a woman a dame.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'if need be' means if it is required, describing something unavoidable.

clue.text: Writer's function and aim

parts.note: a ball is a formal social function, a dance
point means aim, as in point a gun

explanation.surface: Musing on what an author is for and wants to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' reads as possessive, but the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, an instrument that writes.

clue.text: Yankee repairman quietly turning over deck

indicators.note: the combined letters are flipped in this down answer

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet
a fitter repairs and installs things
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An American mechanic silently flips a boat's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, FITTER and P make YFITTERP, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn, as in decking the halls, which is making something look pretty.

clue.text: Little plastic models

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: A brief description of small toy figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Little, as an adverb, means not often: 'we see them little' is rarely.

clue.text: Parrots raising racket across wide area

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters are lifted to read upwards
the swindle stretches across, enclosing, the other letters

parts.note: a racket is a scam
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Noisy birds kicking up a din over a broad stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: W and A inside SCAM give SWACAM, which 'raising' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large colourful tropical birds of the parrot family.

clue.text: Australian peach brandy factory employee?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Australian slang for an excellent person or thing
second meaning: someone who fills bottles at a distillery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like fruit for the brandy, but it is the slang sense of something great.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a 'bottler' is a beauty, while literally it is a worker who puts drinks into containers.

clue.text: Motion's opponents won't face rebuke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those against a motion will not be in favour of it
second meaning: British idiom for being due a telling-off

explanation.walkthrough: To 'be for it' is a British idiom meaning to be in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means support a proposal; idiomatically it means about to be punished.

clue.text: Continue to hoard old pennies and shillings for favoured child

indicators.note: the word for continue stores the coins inside it

parts.note: go on means continue
d was the abbreviation for a penny in old British money
s stood for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: A miser keeps saving coins to leave to a favourite child.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence, written £sd.
explanation.definitionFit: A godson is a boy sponsored at baptism, a child a godparent singles out for care.

clue.text: More trouble as head's dismissed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for trouble is removed

parts.note: bother means trouble

explanation.surface: Further problems at school once the headteacher is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional, as in 'there are other options', so it equals further.

clue.text: Dickensian scavenger, he lifted as much as possible?

indicators.note: in a down answer the word is raised to read upwards

parts.note: max is short for maximum

explanation.surface: A Dickens character who scavenges and lifts as much as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer Hexam in Our Mutual Friend fishes corpses from the Thames and robs them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexam is a character in a Dickens novel who scavenges the river for bodies and valuables.

clue.text: With cold, not on various drugs: drink from this

parts.note: C is short for cold on taps
off is the opposite of on
E and E for ecstasy, then pot for cannabis

explanation.surface: A sick, sober person is being told what to drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffeepot is a vessel from which the brew is poured, so the beverage comes out of it.

clue.text: Cause of complaint from lycée? Endless one

indicators.note: the French word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lycée is a French school, an école
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wondering if a French school is the source of an unending illness.
explanation.walkthrough: A lycée is a French secondary school, so the French word for school, ECOLE, minus its last letter gives ECOL.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli bacteria cause food poisoning, a common stomach illness.

clue.text: Conflict that was ended by The Sun

definitions.text: Conflict that was ended by The Sun

parts.words: Conflict that was ended by The Sun
parts.note: the 1967 Arab-Israeli war lasted Monday to Saturday, so the next day, Sunday, came after its end

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' looks like the tabloid newspaper, but it is Sun, short for Sunday, which followed the six days of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1967 war between Israel and its neighbours lasted under a week, from 5 to 10 June.

clue.text: Mammal's four limbs it oddly passed over

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are skipped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An animal's four legs strangely missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Skip the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of 'four limbs it', and keep the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An oribi is a small African antelope, an animal that suckles its young.

clue.text: People moving, and people opposing, keeping bats caged

indicators.note: the opposing voters hold the next word inside them
the crazy word is enclosed, as if behind bars

parts.note: the noes or nos are those who vote against
bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Travellers and protesters keeping bats in cages.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wanderers with no fixed home who travel from place to place.

clue.text: For diversion, try C-list celebrity show

indicators.note: diverting the letters sends them on a different route into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggesting a reality show with minor celebrities for entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC TV contest pairing celebrities with dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC ballroom contest featuring famous people is commonly shortened to its first word.
